correctness.rationale: The exact action on the active pattern is verified from the all-site match definition. For H<K, the inverse image of any exact-K output y consists of precisely q-1 changed-H patterns, because their Fourier support contains H-annihilator characters nontrivial on K and these characters generate the full H-annihilator. This proves G_p=H and exact fibres. Partition of H-invariant colorings and subgroup Möbius inversion prove all transition counts, including the diagonal. Explicit constructions cover all quotients, including C2, C2×C2, C2^r (r>=3), and elements of order >2. The independent exhaustive standard-library checker confirms 349 counting identities on 17 groups/alphabet combinations; finite checks support but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper proves local action and representative existence for strict and diagonal transitions, and already identifies Klein-four obstruction; those are not new. Its inspected main results do not provide the all-H,K exact number of full-memory lazy rules, Möbius matrix, sharp half-proportion, or probability law. The specific Klein-four continuation enumerates endomorphism monoids and generator lengths, but does not provide this all-abelian stabilizer-transition census. Historical priority remains uncertain, particularly via primitive-necklace or aperiodic-coloring terminology. The actual database and literature searches found no direct implication; absence of matches is not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An older result on translation-free necklaces or free regular group actions may imply the sharp one-half bound under another name.
An independently published all-abelian transition-matrix enumeration not indexed in the searched systems would cover the main claim.
The result is not independently audited, and numerical checks cover only small groups.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-parameter quantitative classification of the one-step symmetry-change possibilities of full-memory lazy cellular automata, directly motivated by the 2026 generator-existence theorem. The q-1 fibre law is unexpectedly independent of the lower stabilizer H and yields exact probabilities, a subgroup-lattice algorithm for all entries and a sharp boundary for stabilizer-preserving transitions. It includes arbitrarily large abelian groups and is neither a finite slice nor a routine restatement of the published existence criterion.
